account:
Today has been mostly routine appointments, but there are hints of preparations I do not fully understand. The builder says eight lanterns have been installed in the great hall and has invited me to inspect the lighting tomorrow at 18:00. I approved, and I have now read the updated appointment book confirming it. The builder described it as an inspection requiring only my opinion, not accounts or approvals. I have no evidence that it is for a celebration, though the new lighting could serve a gathering as well as everyday use.

At tea, my neighbour mentioned chatter about decorations or lights at the bakery. They later identified Townsfolk 02 as the source, but said that person also spoke confusingly about a bridge or port change. My neighbour had not seen decorations personally, and said the baker knew of no special occasion. I therefore regard this as unverified gossip, not proof of an event or a connection to the great hall.

The secretary has been maintaining my appointments and has returned both the original and updated books to the appointments chest. No account figures were supplied for today's accounts meeting, and the secretary reported no correspondence or further business delivered. I have asked for the missing figures and for tomorrow's council letters to be set aside. I heard the secretary speak again while I was reading, but could not make out the words. There may simply be ordinary improvements and muddled gossip; I remain curious, but cannot yet say anyone is arranging something behind my back.
